In 'B' Group, This Day, The Court Made The Following:
 Order

This petition is filed by the petitioner/accused under Section 482 of Cr.P.C., for quashing the criminal proceedings in Spl.C.No.113/2020 arising out of Crime No.494/2018 registered by Gundlupete Police station and charge sheeted for the offences punishable under Sections 198 and 420 of Indian Penal Code (hereinafter referred to as 'IPC') and section 3(1)(ix) of SC and ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 (hereinafter referred to as 'Special Act'.)

sentences.text:
2. Heard the arguments of learned counsel for the petitioner, learned HCGP for respondent Nos.1 and 2 and the learned special counsel for respondent No.3.
3.

The case of the prosecution is that J.S.Narayanaswamy, PSI, Mysore, of Director General of POlice, CRE, Cell filed complaint to Gundlupet Police station on 25.11.2018, alleging that the petitioner said to be belonging to NC: 2024:KHC:10677 'Goundar' community and said to be migrated to Gundlupete, Karnataka and had obtained certificate as scheduled caste 'Bhovi'
community, which belongs to scheduled caste and studied in Karnataka.
Thereafter, the petitioner applied for the post of 'Constable' in KSRP and he said to be selected and appointment order was issued and the caste certificate has been sent for verification.
Later, in the written statement it was found that he does not belong to scheduled caste.
Therefore, intimation was given to the District Caste Verification Committee.
Accordingly, District Verification Committee passed an order 7.12.2017 and cancelled the caste certificate dated 30.10.2013.
Thereafter, directed the complainant to file complaint against the petitioner.
Accordingly, complaint and charge sheet was filed, which is under challenge.
4. Learned counsel for the petitioner contended that the petitioner is not claiming any benefit in the Government, except his appointment.
He has already given letter to the authority that he is not taking the job.
However, contended the caste name was altered in the school certificate, in the registry itself by some unknown teacher, by correcting his caste name as NC: 2024:KHC:10677 from 'Goundar' to 'Bhovi'.
Therefore, this is not mistake of the petitioner or parents, but it is done by some unknown teacher.

Also contended, even his sister's school certificate also was changed by the K M Nagaraj vs State Of Karnataka on 14 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/145337862/
2 school authorities as 'scheduled caste -Bhovi' and there is no case and hence prayed for allowing the petition and quash the criminal proceedings.
5.

sentences.text: Per contra, learned HCGP objected the petition contending that the DCVC already annulled the certificate.
He has approached the authority for seeking appointment.

He has been selected and appointed as constable, but when the certificate was sent for verification, it was found, he does not belong to SC community but was appointed and also he has studied in the school with the said certificate.
Therefore, it cannot be said he is not availing any benefit from the government and it is a triable case.
Learned special counsel also relied upon the judgment in Crl.P.No.2346 .
Hence, prayed for dismissing the case.
6. Having heard the arguments and perused records.

On perusal of the same, the allegation against the petitioner is that he has filed application for the constable post for recruitment NC:
2024:KHC:10677 conducted by the KSRP.
Accordingly, he said to be selected under the reservation category.
He has produced the School Certificate and Transfer Certificate as Scheduled Caste-'Bhovi'.
The documents are also produced before the court.

The school certificate especially the school register maintained by the school at Gundlupet, reveals he has been admitted in the first standard and date of birth was shown as 3.5.1987 and in the category of the caste column, the caste was mentioned as 'Gounder' and altered as 'Bhovi'.
Thereafter, the petitioner studied and completed Degree.
Likewise his sister also had obtained the caste certificate, which reveals her caste name is 'Agambadi Goundar' but it was rounded and mentioned as 'Bhovi'.
Learned counsel for the petitioner submits, it is not the mistake of the petitioner or his parents, but it is written by some unknown school teacher as per the letter shown by the school authority.
Whether, he belongs to Bhovi community or SC community, it is personally known to the petitioner and his family.

If at all the petitioner belongs to the 'Bhovi' community in Karnataka even Goundar community in Tamil Nadu which comes under the SC category he has to prove the same before the Trial Court and justify their caste name appearing in the NC: 2024:KHC:10677 caste certficate.
However, the DCVC has already made an enquiry and annulled the certificate on 6.1.2014.
Presently, it reveals the petitioner does not belongs to SC community, but belongs to 'Goundar' which comes under OBC category but not SC reservation category.

Learned counsel for the petitioner submits, they have not obtained any benefit by taking the reservation, but the petitioner and sister have studies in the said reservation category and completed education.
Such being the case, it cannot he said they have not claimed any benefit out of the reservation.

That apart, he has also applied the post for constable by showing the Bhovi caste certificate and also got the appointment was received and before reporting to the job a verification has been made by the authority on 6.1.2014 certificate has been anulled.

Thereafter, the petitioner said to be given letter which sought intention for jointing the post due to his family problem and the letter of petitioner was dated 04.09.2014, but not prior to his appointing or filing application for appointment.
Such being the case, it cannot be said he has not obtained any benefit or appointed under the reservation category.

In a similar situation, the coordinate bench of this court in SRI MADHUKAR v. STATE NC: 2024:KHC:10677 BY HOSANAGARA POLICE AND ANOTHER in Crl.P.No.2346/2014 has held by relying upon the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of "Shoba Lakshmi Vs Divisional Commissioner & Ors (In Spl Leave to Appeal (Civil) No.138/2013 dated 28.01.2013) and dismissed the petition on the ground, the proceeding can be initiated, as per the rule 7-A of the Karnataka Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes and other K M Nagaraj vs State Of Karnataka on 14 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/145337862/

sentences.text: Said certificates were cancelled by the CRE Cell.
In order steer clear from the impending prosecution, petitioner therein took shelter under the aforesaid order of Government dated 11th March 2002.

However, the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the above decision ratified the NC: 2024:KHC:10677 view taken by the Division Bench of this Court which reads as under:-
"Be that as it may, there was certain confusion in regard to treating 'Maleru' and 'Maaleru' as Scheduled Tribe.

The said fact has been settled stating that 'Maleru'
alone belongs to Scheduled Tribe and not 'Maaleru'.

A Co-ordinate Bench of this Court in W.A.No.4023/2004 and other connected writ appeals has decided that 'Maaleru' does not belong to Scheduled Tribe and that such candidates cannot claim the benefit of Scheduled Tribe and therefore, the said question is no more a integra.

The judgment relied upon by the learned counsel for the appellant in Union of India vs. H. Ramakrishna is also not helpful to the appellant in view of the subsequent judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court which are relied upon by the learned counsel for the appellant.

sentences.text: When the order of the State Government cannot be extended to the central Government Employees as NC: 2024:KHC:10677 ruled by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Addl.
General Manager-Human Resources, Bharat Heavy Electricals Ltd., vs. Suresh Ramkrishna Burde ((2007) 5 SCC 336].

sentences.text: It is clear that the appellant cannot contend that in view of the order of the Government dated 11th March 2002, the appellant's appointment has been saved because the Parliament has not declared 'Maaleru' as Scheduled Tribe to save the appointment of the appellant based on the order of the State of Karnataka.

In addition to that, by the order of the State a right vested under Articles 341 and 342 of the Constitution of India cannot be diluted and cannot be taken away."
(underline supplied) Whether criminal prosecution could be launched against imposters who by posing themselves as members of the caste, tribe or class for whom reservation has been earmarked has been considered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of KUMARI MADHURI PATIL vs.

sentences.text: "A prosecution should be launched against the candidate or, as the case may be, the parents or guardians responsible for making the false claim.
The regime postulated in the judgment of this Court in Madhuri Patil (supra) took effect from 2 September 1994, which was the date of the judgment.
Eventually in the State of Maharashtra these directions received legislative recognition upon the enactment of the Maharashtra Act XXIII of 2001 which came into force in the State on 18 October 2001.

However, it is important to notice that even before the State Legislature stepped in to confer a statutory form to the directions which were issued by this Court in Madhuri Patil (supra) the regime, as it then obtained prior to the enactment of the - 11 - NC: 2024:KHC:10677 law, also envisaged consequences upon a caste or tribe claim being found to be false upon a verification by the Scrutiny Committee.
The cancellation of a certificate would, as a necessary consequence, involve the invalidation of the appointment to a post or admission to an educational institution.

Where a candidate had been appointed to a reserved post on the basis of the claim that he or she was a member of the group for which the reservation is intended, the invalidation of the claim to belong to that group would, as a necessary consequence,
render the appointment void ab initio.

The rationale for this is that a candidate who would otherwise have to compete for a post in the general pool of unreserved seats had secured appointment in a more restricted competition confined to the reserved category and usurped a benefit meant for a designated caste, tribe or class.

Once it was found that the candidate had obtained admission upon a false representation to belong to the reserved - 12 - NC: 2024:KHC:10677 category, the appointment would be vitiated by fraud and would be void ab initio.
The falsity of the claim lies in a representation that the candidate belongs to a category of persons for whom the reservation is intended whereas in fact the candidate does not so belong.

The reason for depriving the candidate of the benefit which she or he has obtained on the strength of such a claim,
is that a person cannot retain the fruits of a false claim on the basis of which a scarce public resource is obtained.
The same principle would apply where a candidate secures admission to an educational institution on the basis of a false claim to belong to a reserved category.
A candidate who does so causes detriment to a genuine candidate who actually belongs to the reserved category who is deprived of the seat.

For that matter a detriment is caused to the entire class of persons for whom reservations are intended, the members of which are excluded as a result of an admission granted to an imposter who does not - 13 - K M Nagaraj vs State Of Karnataka on 14 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/145337862/
5 NC: 2024:KHC:10677 belong to the class.

entities.text: K M Nagaraj vs State Of Karnataka
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The withdrawal of benefits, either in terms of the revocation of employment or the termination of an admission was hence a necessary corollary of the invalidation of the claim on the basis of which the appointment or admission was obtained.
The withdrawal of the benefit was not based on mens rea or the intent underlying the assertion of a false claim.
In the case of a criminal prosecution, intent would be necessary.
On the other hand, the withdrawal of civil benefits flowed as a logical result of the invalidation of a claim to belong to a group or category for whom the reservations is intended.
This was the position under the regime which prevailed following the decision in Madhuri Patil."

Further, in para 53 of the said order, it is observed as under:-
 "Administrative circulars and  Government resolutions are subservient to legislative mandate and cannot be contrary either to - 14 - NC: 2024:KHC:10677 constitutional norms or statutory principles.

Where a candidate has obtained an appointment to a post on the solemn basis that he or she belongs to a designated caste, tribe or class for whom the post is meant and it is found upon verification by the Scrutiny Committee that the claim is false, the services of such an individual cannot be protected by taking recourse to administrative circulars or resolutions.
Protection of claims of a usurper is an act of deviance to the constitutional scheme as well as to statutory mandate.
No government resolution or circular can override constitutional or statutory norms.
The principle that government is bound by its own circulars is well- settled but it cannot apply in a situation such as present.

Protecting the services of a candidate who is found not to belong to the community or tribe for whom the reservation is intended substantially encroaches upon legal rights of genuine members of the reserved communities whose - 15 - NC: 2024:KHC:10677 just entitlements are negated by the grant of a seat to an ineligible person.

In such a situation where the rights of genuine members of reserved groups or communities are liable to be affected detrimentally, government circulars or resolutions cannot operate to their detriment."

Lastly, Rule 7-A of The Karnataka Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes and Other Backward (Reservations of Appointment, Etc.,) Rules, 1992 specifically provides for prosecution of the offenders who obtained false caste certificate.

Said Rule reads as under:
7-A. Prosecution for obtaining false caste certificate-(1) The Caste Verification Committee or the Caste and Income Verification Committee, as the case may be and the Divisional Commissioner, shall send a copy of the order rejecting claim of the K M Nagaraj vs State Of Karnataka on 14 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/145337862/
6 applicant for grant of Validity Certificate or, as the case may be, a Copy of the order in appeal - 16 - NC: 2024:KHC:10677 rejecting such claim, to the Directorate of Civil Rights Enforcement.
(2) The Directorate of Civil Rights Enforcement shall take steps to prosecute such claimant who has obtained a false Caste Certificate."
Based upon the judgment, this court also dismissed the petition in similar case, where the parents of the employee misused the caste certificate by inserting the caste name of the their son in the school while admitting the children.

Accordingly, this petition is dismissed Sd/-
